description:
Add server-side Round 1 ('To Live') team-assignment logic in engine.py and expose it via a thin PUT /api/round1-assign endpoint in app.py, mirroring the existing round2_draw_action + /api/round2-draw pattern. One wheel spin picks an as-yet-unassigned Round 1 player and immediately assigns them to Team A or Team B by a true, unbiased coin flip using the `secrets` module, capped so once a side reaches 5 the remaining players go to the other side -- the logic ALWAYS terminates at a valid 5/5 split. The server also tracks which Round 1 players were assigned by the wheel (vs manually via the dropdown) so a 'reset' action can clear exactly the wheel-assigned teams. Manual override of team via the existing round1.players.

.team dropdown must keep working and must coexist with wheel assignments. Keep schema version 4 and keep validate()/migrate() accepting old saves that lack the new field. Add unit tests. Doing the randomness server-side (not only in JS) is the established, strongly-preferred pattern because it is unit-testable.
steps: In engine.py, extend the Round 1 state to track wheel-assigned players. Add a `round1_assigned` list of player IDs (ids assigned by the wheel). Put it on the round1 stage object: update blank_round(5) so the round1 stage includes `'assigned': []` (only for the 5-game/round1 shape; blank_round(8) for round2 must NOT get this field). Confirm new_state() therefore seeds round1.assigned=[].

In engine.py validate(): default a missing round1.assigned to [] (so older version-4 saves and migrated v1/v2/v3 saves still validate). Validate that round1['assigned'] is a list of unique IDs all in IDS, and that every id in it currently has a non-empty team ('A' or 'B'). Reject invalid shapes with a clear ValueError consistent with the existing messages. Ensure migrate() output still passes validate() for v1/v2/v3 fixtures.

In engine.py add round1_assign_action(s, action): deepcopy s like round2_draw_action does. For action=='spin': find Round 1 players with team=='' (unassigned, in IDS order); if none remain, return s unchanged (idempotent, like round2 'start' repeat-click guard). Otherwise pick the next unassigned player -- the ORDER a specific player is drawn is a UI concern, so for determinism/testability select candidates in IDS order (the UI decides which physical slice the wheel lands on; the server just assigns the next unassigned player a team). Count current A and B among ALL round1 players. If A has 5 already, assign 'B'; if B has 5 already, assign 'A'; otherwise flip a true unbiased coin with secrets (e.g. secrets.randbelow(2)) to choose 'A' or 'B'. Set that player's team and append the id to round1['assigned']. For action=='reset': clear teams for every id in round1['assigned'] (set team='') and set round1['assigned']=[]. Reset must NOT touch manually-set teams (ids not in the assigned list). Raise ValueError('Unknown Round 1 assignment action.') for anything else. Return the state (no bind_rosters needed for round1 since round1 is the top of the chain, but calling evaluate is unnecessary; keep it simple).

Important cap-correctness detail: because each spin assigns exactly one unassigned player and the cap forces the deficient side once either side hits 5, after all 10 players are assigned the split is always exactly 5 A / 5 B. Make the implementation robust to a starting state that already has some manual A/B assignments (e.g. user manually set 3 to A, then spins the rest): the cap must still count existing manual assignments so it never exceeds 5 on a side. If manual assignments already make a valid 5/5 impossible is not something spin can fix; spin only assigns unassigned players and respects the 5-cap, so if manual input already put 6 on one side the dropdown validation/round1_view surfaces that -- spin itself must never push a side past 5.

In app.py do_PUT: add '/api/round1-assign' to the allowed PUT routes list alongside '/api/state' and '/api/round2-draw'. When self.path=='/api/round1-assign', after the token + revision checks, call store.save(round1_assign_action(store.state, data['action'])) . Use the default allow_draw=False (Round 1 assignment does not touch the round2 draw, so the draw-guard in Store.save is unaffected). Import round1_assign_action from engine at the top of app.py next to the other engine imports.

Add unit tests in tests/test_tournament.py (new test methods in the Rules or a new class). Cover: (a) repeatedly spinning from a fresh new_state() with 10 blank teams always yields exactly 5 on A and 5 on B, and all 10 ids end up in round1['assigned']; run this many times (e.g. 200 iterations) to exercise the random coin flip. (b) The cap: patch engine.secrets to force an extreme bias (e.g. always return 0 so coin always says 'A') and confirm the result is STILL 5 A / 5 B (first 5 go to A, the cap forces the rest to B). (c) assigned players are excluded from future spins: after a player is assigned, another spin never reassigns them and never changes a team already set; the count of assigned grows by exactly 1 per spin until 10. (d) reset: after a full wheel assignment, round1_assign_action(s,'reset') clears all teams and empties round1['assigned']; and reset does NOT clear a team that was set manually (set one team manually, assign the rest by wheel, reset, confirm the manual one survives and only wheel ones cleared). (e) manual override coexists: assign all by wheel to reach 5/5, then manually flip one player's team via s['round1']['players'][p]['team'] and confirm validate() still accepts it. (f) a fresh spin respects pre-existing manual assignments and never exceeds 5 per side. (g) backward-compat: a saved state dict lacking round1['assigned'] passes validate() and gets defaulted to []. Follow the existing test style (fixture()/new_state(), unittest.mock.patch on engine.secrets like test_balanced_random_draw_all_matches_and_repeat_clicks patches engine.secrets.SystemRandom.shuffle).
Run the full suite and confirm all tests (old + new) pass.
acceptance_criteria: engine.round1_assign_action(new_state(), 'spin') called until no unassigned players remain always produces exactly 5 players with team 'A' and 5 with team 'B', across many randomized runs.
When engine.secrets is patched so the coin flip always returns the same side, the 5-per-side cap still forces a valid 5/5 split (no side ever exceeds 5).
A player assigned by the wheel is recorded in round1['assigned'] and is never re-assigned by a later spin; each spin assigns exactly one previously-unassigned player.
round1_assign_action(s,'reset') sets team='' only for ids in round1['assigned'] and empties round1['assigned'], leaving manually-set teams untouched.

Manually setting a player's team via the dropdown path (round1.players.

.team) still validates and coexists with wheel assignments.
validate() defaults a missing round1['assigned'] to [] so pre-existing version-4 saves and migrated v1/v2/v3 saves still load.
PUT /api/round1-assign with {action:'spin'} and {action:'reset'} works end to end through the running server and persists to tournament.json.
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` passes with the new tests included and no regressions.
verification: Single-invocation server test: start app.py --no-browser on a port, GET /api/state for token+revision, PUT /api/round1-assign {action:'spin'} ten times driving a full assignment, assert the final state has exactly 5 team A and 5 team B, then PUT {action:'reset'} and assert all round1 teams are cleared; kill the server. (wrap in one script under /projects/sandbox)
findings: Implemented round1_assign_action(s, action) in engine.py mirroring round2_draw_action (deepcopy, no bind_rosters needed for round1). blank_round(5) now seeds 'assigned':[]; blank_round(8) does not. validate() defaults a missing round1['assigned'] to [] via setdefault and checks it is a list of unique IDS whose teams are 'A'/'B'. Spin selects the first unassigned player in IDS order, counts ALL current A/B (manual + wheel), forces the deficient side at the 5-cap, else flips secrets.randbelow(2); returns s unchanged when nothing is unassigned (idempotent). Reset clears team only for ids in round1['assigned'] and empties the list. app.py: imported round1_assign_action, added '/api/round1-assign' to the allowed PUT list, routed it to store.save(round1_assign_action(...)) with default allow_draw=False. Added Round1Assign test class (7 tests incl. 200 randomized runs + forced-bias cap for both coin sides) and an HTTP endpoint test. Full suite 33 passing (was 24). Server smoke test (one-shot script) drove 10 spins to a 5A/5B split and a reset to all-cleared. node tests/test_ui.cjs still passes.
